expected.note: WordPress behind MariaDB (ff-wp-db), reachable on 8090. Added 2026-11-24 so the four WP2Shell variants have a victim that runs the application the CVE is in; without it those variants were enforced against nothing.

mod_php victim for PHP2Shell. session.upload_progress.cleanup=Off and an LFI sink (/vuln.php) were added deliberately: chain A needs both, and the defaults made it return an empty body. Recorded in data/lab/poc-runs/.
mod_proxy_fcgi enablereuse=on; effect not observed here

php:8.4.26-apache with the reference lab's session.serialize_handler=php_serialize + upload-progress-on configuration and its LabGadget app (lab/php-115560/). Built because ff-php cannot host this CVE: its global handler is already `php`, so the serialiser the advisory says writes the session never runs and a null result there would prove nothing.
the same image and app with session.upload_progress.enabled=0 (the vendor mitigation), so the RCE can be shown to depend on that one setting rather than on the container

built 2026-11-26 from lab/php-129474/Containerfile: the fleet's php is 8.4.26, outside this CVE's 8.5.0..8.5.12 range, so the victim is built at 8.5.12 with zend.exception_ignore_args=Off (the config whose argument collection the CVE corrupts).
same image and app with zend.exception_ignore_args=On - the vendor's own mitigation, run against to show the collected-arguments behaviour comes from that setting.
the patched engine php:8.5.13-apache with the same app - the fix side of the victim pair.

built 2026-11-26 from lab/php-129496/Containerfile: the fleet's own engine image (php:8.4.26-apache is exactly what ff-php runs, and 8.4.26 is inside this CVE's 8.4.*<8.4.28 range) plus the advisory's config pair - file error_log + unresolvable date.timezone - and memory_limit=2M as the reference labs set. Built as its own container because ff-php has a valid timezone and no PHP file log, so the bug's precondition cannot exist there and a null would prove nothing (see lab/php-129496/README.md).

the same image and app with date.timezone=Etc/UTC - the vendor's first mitigation (the setting whose invalid value prints at startup). The same oversized POST must be answered (memory fatal) instead of killing the worker: the causality control for the entry.
the patched engine php:8.4.28-apache with the same app and the same vulnerable ini - the fix side of the victim pair (measured: answers the POST with the memory fatal, worker alive).
MariaDB for the two Drupal victims with max-connections=25 - the pool size the Fail2Install write-up calls its reliable reproduction config; not port-published, same convention as ff-wp-db.

provisioned 2026-11-28 via lab/drupal-132165/provision.sh: the affected 11.4.x release (NVD range 11.4.0..11.4.13 lessThan - the image is that range's last affected release) installed against drupal_v with drush, the state the CVE attacks (an installed site whose core/install.php still answers). The write-up's exact image+version pairing.

the fixed release, same provisioning and the second database (drupal_p): for this CVE the fix does not remove the reachable installer (measured: same 200 'Drupal already installed' answer), which is why the vendor still tells every site to block it - the fact the twin exists to show.
